name: Aardwolf Players
author: Solao
description: Who list with per-player whois and finger, a searchable history and timed sweeps.
script:
--[[
    aw-who.lua
    Sean Stoves (Solao) — 2026-08-05

    Player tracker. Reads 'who' output, keeps a record of everyone it has ever
    seen, and can sweep on a timer with the output gagged.

    Parsing happens in onLine rather than in triggers, and that is not a style
    choice: a line discarded from onLine fires no triggers at all, so a gagged
    sweep would be an invisible one. Both jobs have to happen in the same pass.

    Nothing here needs GMCP. Aardwolf has no who package — the list only exists
    as text, which is why this is a parser and not a subscription.
]]

plugin = {
    id          = "aw-who",
    name        = "Aardwolf Players",
    version     = "1.13.5",
    author      = "Solao",
    description = "Who list with per-player whois and finger, a searchable history and timed sweeps.",
    settings    = { saveState = true },
}

--[[
    Drop every handler already on a widget event.

    Looked up through _G rather than called by name: a global this build does
    not have throws on the way IN, before pcall can catch anything, so a bare
    reference would take the plugin down on any client that lacks it.
]]
local function drop_handlers(id, event)
    local ok, fn = pcall(function() return _G["unregisterWidgetEvent"] end)
    if ok and type(fn) == "function" then pcall(fn, id, event) end
end


-- @category widgets

local TAG  = "$Y[Who v" .. plugin.version .. "]$w "
local TAGR = "$R[Who v" .. plugin.version .. "]$w "

local DB_FILE    = "aw-who.json"
local SWEEP_FILE = "aw-who-sweep.json"
local VAR        = "aw_who_db"
local SWEEP_VAR  = "aw_who_sweep"

local MAX_ROWS = 80          -- rendered at once; search is how you reach the rest

local widget = nil
local view   = "list"        -- "list" | "settings"

--[[
    Everyone ever seen, keyed by lowercased name. The sweep list is separate
    and holds only the most recent one: "online" means "in the last sweep",
    which is a claim we can actually support.
]]
-- players live in buckets now, not one table: see the split below
local sweep   = { names = {}, at = 0, found = 0, max = 0, conns = 0 }

local inSweep = false        -- between the header and the footer
local tail    = false        -- past the footer, still inside the block
local auto    = false        -- this sweep is ours, so gag it
local dirty   = false

--[[
    Instrumentation. The first version parsed nothing and looked exactly like a
    sweep that found nobody — no error, no clue. These say whether onLine is
    being called at all and whether the header was recognised, which are the
    two things that were silently false.
]]
local dbg = { lines = 0, heads = 0, rows = 0, errs = 0, last = "" }

local cfg = {
    poll  = false,           -- sweep on a timer
    mins  = 15,              -- minutes between sweeps
    gag   = true,            -- hide the output of our own sweeps
    query = "",              -- current search
}

------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- helpers. every one of these exists because of something the Lua-to-JS
-- boundary does differently; see docs/MUDFORGE-NOTES.md
------------------------------------------------------------------------------

local function str(v)
    if type(v) ~= "string" then return nil end
    if v == "" or v == "undefined" or v == "null" then return nil end
    return v
end

--[[
    A field that survived the broken parser.

    JS undefined is truthy under Lua rules, so `p.class or ""` kept it and
    string.gsub wrote the literal text "undefined" into the database. Records
    saved before 1.3.0 carry it, and it would show forever otherwise.
]]
local function clean_field(v)
    return str(v) or ""
end

local function num(v)
    local n = tonumber(v)
    if type(n) ~= "number" then return nil end
    if n ~= n then return nil end
    return n
end

local function trim(s)
    if type(s) ~= "string" then return "" end

    local a = 1
    while a <= string.len(s) and string.sub(s, a, a) == " " do a = a + 1 end

    local b = string.len(s)
    while b >= a and string.sub(s, b, b) == " " do b = b - 1 end

    return string.sub(s, a, b)
end

-- split on whitespace by hand: Lua character classes don't survive the JS
-- regex engine, and this runs on every line of a hundred-player sweep
local function words(s)
    local out, cur = {}, ""

    for i = 1, string.len(s) do
        local c = string.sub(s, i, i)
        if c == " " or c == "\t" then
            if cur ~= "" then table.insert(out, cur); cur = "" end
        else
            cur = cur .. c
        end
    end

    if cur ~= "" then table.insert(out, cur) end
    return out
end

local function esc(s)
    if type(s) ~= "string" then return "" end
    s = string.gsub(s, "&", "&")
    s = string.gsub(s, "<", "<")
    s = string.gsub(s, ">", ">")
    s = string.gsub(s, '"', """)
    return s
end

local function commas(n)
    if type(n) ~= "number" then return "0" end

    local s, out, c = tostring(math.floor(n)), "", 0
    for i = string.len(s), 1, -1 do
        out = string.sub(s, i, i) .. out
        c = c + 1
        if c % 3 == 0 and i > 1 then out = "," .. out end
    end
    return out
end

local function key_of(name)
    return string.lower(trim(name or ""))
end

------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- storage
------------------------------------------------------------------------------

--[[
    Hand-built JSON, read back with json.decode. Same reasoning as the SnD
    database: an encoder's behaviour on nested arrays across the transpiler is
    the sort of thing that has bitten repeatedly here.

    Mirrored into a world variable because saveTable and savePluginFile are
    both scoped to the plugin, and a remove-and-re-add — how every update is
    installed — takes them with it.
]]
--[[
    Per-world, which is the default scope.

    These were written with scope "global" — one namespace shared by every
    character on every world. A database of Aardwolf players has no business
    being visible on a different MUD, and the default store is that world's
    own file: isolated between worlds, still shared by every plugin on the
    same one, so anything that wants to read this can.

    read_world() falls back to the old app-wide copy once, so nothing already
    collected disappears the day the scope changes.
]]
local function read_world(file)
    local raw = loadPluginFile(file)
    if type(raw) == "string" and raw ~= "" then return raw end

    --[[
        The old app-wide copy, read by hand rather than through this function.

        A blanket rewrite of loadPluginFile(x, "global") -> read_world(x)
        caught this line too, so read_world called itself and every load ended
        in 'Maximum call stack size exceeded' before a single line of the
        plugin ran.
    ]]
    local old = loadPluginFile(file, "global")
    if type(old) == "string" and old ~= "" then
        pcall(savePluginFile, file, old)
        return old
    end

    return nil
end

--[[
    The player database is split by first letter.

    It used to be one file and one world variable holding every player ever
    seen, decoded whole at every startup. RAM cost here is the size of the keys
    you touch, not the size of the database — and the key is the only thing
    that can narrow a read, since the store gives us whole values by name and
    nothing finer. So the key does the work a WHERE clause would.

    Two buckets are held at most. A lookup goes straight to the letter it needs;
    a search walks them one at a time and lets each go.
]]
local BUCKETS_HELD = 2

local bkt      = {}       -- letter -> { key -> player }
local bktDirty = {}       -- letter -> true
local bktUsed  = {}       -- letter -> counter, newest highest
local bktTick  = 0
local playerN  = 0

local BUCKETS = { "0", "_" }
for i = 0, 25 do table.insert(BUCKETS, string.char(97 + i)) end

--[[
    Scanned by hand. '%a' is a Lua character class and these patterns run on a
    JavaScript regex engine, where it matches nothing — in the loot tracker
    that silently filed every row into one bucket, which is the whole scheme
    not working while looking like it did.
]]
local function bucket_of(key)
    for i = 1, string.len(key) do
        local c = string.sub(key, i, i)
        if c >= "a" and c <= "z" then return c end
        if c >= "0" and c <= "9" then return "0" end
    end
    return "_"
end

local function bkt_file(letter) return "aw-who-" .. letter .. ".json" end
local function bkt_var(letter)  return "aw_who_db_" .. letter end

local function encode_rows(t)
    local out = {}
    for _, p in pairs(t) do
        table.insert(out, '{"n":"' .. string.gsub(p.name, '"', "")
            .. '","l":' .. tostring(p.level or 0)
            .. ',"r":"' .. string.gsub(clean_field(p.race), '"', "")
            .. '","c":"' .. string.gsub(clean_field(p.class), '"', "")
            .. '","t":"' .. string.gsub(clean_field(p.title), '"', "")
            .. '","g":"' .. string.gsub(clean_field(p.flags), '"', "")
            .. '","s":' .. tostring(p.seen or 1)
            .. ',"a":' .. tostring(p.at or 0) .. "}")
    end
    return "[" .. table.concat(out, ",") .. "]"
end

local function decode_rows(raw, into)
    if type(raw) ~= "string" or raw == "" then return 0 end

    local ok, data = pcall(json.decode, raw)
    if not ok or type(data) ~= "table" then return 0 end

    local n = 0
    for _, r in pairs(data) do
        if type(r) == "table" and str(r.n) then
            into[key_of(r.n)] = {
                name  = r.n,
                level = num(r.l) or 0,
                race  = clean_field(r.r),
                class = clean_field(r.c),
                title = clean_field(r.t),
                flags = clean_field(r.g),
                badge = clean_field(r.b),
                clan  = clean_field(r.k),
                seen  = num(r.s) or 1,
                at    = num(r.a) or 0,
            }
            n = n + 1
        end
    end
    return n
end

local function evict()
    local held = {}
    for letter in pairs(bkt) do table.insert(held, letter) end
    if #held <= BUCKETS_HELD then return end

    table.sort(held, function(a, b) return (bktUsed[a] or 0) > (bktUsed[b] or 0) end)

    for i = BUCKETS_HELD + 1, #held do
        local letter = held[i]
        if not bktDirty[letter] then      -- never drop unsaved rows
            bkt[letter] = nil
            bktUsed[letter] = nil
        end
    end
end

local function load_bucket(letter)
    bktTick = bktTick + 1
    bktUsed[letter] = bktTick

    if bkt[letter] then return bkt[letter] end

    local t = {}
    local raw = read_world(bkt_file(letter))

    -- the plugin's own file is gone after a reinstall; the variable isn't
    if type(raw) ~= "string" or raw == "" then
        local ok, back = pcall(function() return getVariable(bkt_var(letter)) end)
        if ok and type(back) == "string" then raw = back end
    end

    decode_rows(raw, t)
    bkt[letter] = t

    evict()
    return t
end

local function get_player(key)
    return load_bucket(bucket_of(key))[key]
end

local function put_player(key, row)
    local letter = bucket_of(key)
    local t = load_bucket(letter)

    if t[key] == nil then playerN = playerN + 1 end
    t[key] = row
    bktDirty[letter] = true
end

local function save_db()
    if not dirty then return end

    for letter in pairs(bktDirty) do
        local blob = encode_rows(bkt[letter] or {})
        savePluginFile(bkt_file(letter), blob)
        pcall(function() setVariable(bkt_var(letter), blob) end)
    end

    bktDirty = {}
    dirty = false

    saveTable("aw_who_meta", { count = playerN })
    evict()
end

--[[
    Carry the old single-file database into buckets, once.

    Everything used to live in one aw-who.json (and one world variable), which
    is exactly what the split is for. Anything already collected would
    otherwise still be on disk and unreadable, which looks like the tracker
    having forgotten every player you have ever seen.
]]
local function load_db()
    local meta = loadTable("aw_who_meta")
    if type(meta) == "table" then
        playerN = num(meta.count) or 0
        if playerN > 0 then return playerN end       -- already split
    end

    local raw = read_world(DB_FILE)
    if type(raw) ~= "string" or raw == "" then
        local ok, back = pcall(function() return getVariable(VAR) end)
        if ok and type(back) == "string" then raw = back end
    end

    local all = {}
    local n = decode_rows(raw, all)
    if n == 0 then return 0 end

    for key, row in pairs(all) do
        local letter = bucket_of(key)
        local t = load_bucket(letter)
        if t[key] == nil then playerN = playerN + 1 end
        t[key] = row
        bktDirty[letter] = true
    end

    dirty = true
    save_db()

    utilprint(TAG .. "split " .. commas(n) .. " player record(s) into buckets.")
    return n
end

--[[
    The last sweep, kept across reloads.

    Without this the panel comes back empty and reads ONLINE 0 until you
    remember to sweep again — the records were all still there, but the one
    list you actually look at was gone. "Online" still means "in the most
    recent sweep"; that sweep is just allowed to have happened yesterday.
]]
local function save_sweep()
    local names = {}
    for _, n in ipairs(sweep.names) do
        table.insert(names, '"' .. string.gsub(n, '"', "") .. '"')
    end

    local blob = '{"n":[' .. table.concat(names, ",") .. "]"
        .. ',"at":' .. tostring(num(sweep.at) or 0)
        .. ',"f":' .. tostring(num(sweep.found) or 0)
        .. ',"m":' .. tostring(num(sweep.max) or 0)
        .. ',"c":' .. tostring(num(sweep.conns) or 0) .. "}"

    savePluginFile(SWEEP_FILE, blob)
    pcall(function() setVariable(SWEEP_VAR, blob) end)
end

local function load_sweep()
    local raw = read_world(SWEEP_FILE)

    if type(raw) ~= "string" or raw == "" then
        local ok, back = pcall(function() return getVariable(SWEEP_VAR) end)
        if ok and type(back) == "string" then raw = back end
    end

    if type(raw) ~= "string" or raw == "" then return end

    local ok, d = pcall(json.decode, raw)
    if not ok or type(d) ~= "table" then return end

    sweep.names = {}
    if type(d.n) == "table" then
        for _, n in pairs(d.n) do
            if str(n) then table.insert(sweep.names, n) end
        end
    end

    sweep.at    = num(d.at) or 0
    sweep.found = num(d.f) or 0
    sweep.max   = num(d.m) or 0
    sweep.conns = num(d.c) or 0
end

local function save_cfg()
    saveTable("aw_who", cfg)
    pcall(function()
        setVariable("aw_who_cfg", '{"poll":' .. (cfg.poll and "true" or "false")
            .. ',"mins":' .. tostring(cfg.mins)
            .. ',"gag":' .. (cfg.gag and "true" or "false") .. "}")
    end)
end

------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- parsing
------------------------------------------------------------------------------

--[[
    Flags that sit in front of the name, as literals rather than patterns —
    plain string comparison beats a regex when every one of them is fixed text.
]]
local FLAGS = {
    "*AFK*", "(OPK)", "(HARDCORE)", "(Linkdead)", "*[AFK]*", "(TRAITOR)",
    "(RAIDER)", "(WANTED)", "(Note)", "(Answer)", "(Editor)", "(DUEL)", "-Idle-",
}

--[[
    Clan decorations, and which clan each one means.

    Carried over from the Mudlet tracker, where it was worked out against
    293,554 real who rows. Two things in it are not obvious:

    The RIGHTMOST match wins. A clan tag trails the title, and a title can name
    a different clan — "Erikson was kidnapped from -=*)Dragon(*=- by [Emerald]"
    is Emerald, and taking the first match filed him under Dragon.

    There is deliberately no Dragon entry. 'clist' has 27 clans and Dragon
    isn't one, so nobody can be wearing it; it only ever appears inside other
    people's titles, which is the row above.
]]
local DECOR = {
    { "|| BOOT ||", "boot" },   { "}HooK{", "hook" },       { ")light(", "light" },
    { "(Seekers)", "seekers" }, { "[Emerald]", "emerald" }, { "[Ba'al]", "baal" },
    { "-=Masaki=-", "masaki" }, { "winlobe", "twinlobe" },  { "|Watchmen|", "watchmen" },
    { "TouchStone", "touchstone" }, { "imson|", "crimson" }, { "erdition", "perdition" },
    { "aardian|", "gaardian" }, { "Loqui|", "loqui" },      { "/Pyre", "pyre" },
    { "IMPERIUM", "imperium" }, { "ibution-", "retribution" }, { "[Loner]", "loner" },
    { "|Wolf|", "wolf" },       { "}Tao{", "tao" },         { "/|\\", "druid" },
    { "Rhabdo/", "rhabdo" },    { "<*]AMAZON[*>", "amazon" }, { "=Crusader=", "crusader" },
    { "o/~ Bard ~\\o", "bard" },
}

local function starts_with(s, pre)
    return string.sub(s, 1, string.len(pre)) == pre
end

--[[
    Rightmost occurrence of a literal, by comparison. No string.find, no
    pattern, no flags.

    string.find's plain argument cannot be relied on here, and several of the
    decorations below are actively hostile as patterns: '|| BOOT ||' is
    alternation with empty branches, which matches at every position, and
    '/|\\' ends in a dangling backslash. Either way the search stops advancing
    and the client locks up with nothing to read afterwards.

    Walking backwards also gets the rightmost hit directly, which is what the
    caller wants, instead of scanning forward and keeping the last one.
]]
--[[
    Leading run of letters, by hand.

    string.match(title, "^([A-Za-z]+)\\b") returned nil on almost every line
    and "a" on one — \\b is not reliable here and a multi-capture match doesn't
    hand back what it should. One player parsed out of two hundred and fifty.
]]
local function lead_word(s)
    local out = ""

    for i = 1, string.len(s) do
        local c = string.sub(s, i, i)
        if (c >= "a" and c <= "z") or (c >= "A" and c <= "Z") then
            out = out .. c
        else
            break
        end
    end

    if out == "" then return nil end
    return out
end

local function rfind(hay, needle)
    local hl, nl = string.len(hay), string.len(needle)
    if nl == 0 or nl > hl then return nil end

    for i = hl - nl + 1, 1, -1 do
        if string.sub(hay, i, i + nl - 1) == needle then return i end
    end

    return nil
end

--[[
    One who line:

        [ 36  Cent   Ran] BlastFomer holds nothing sacred x|| BOOT ||x[C]
        [***ROADHOUSE***] Fertain not a barbarian .:::|Loqui|:::.[C]
        [  1  Human  T+7] (OPK) Haladin
        [ 12  Human  Thi] (Linkdead) TheBlackRose the Bandit

    Fixed columns, not a regex: the bracket is exactly positions 1 and 17, and
    trusting that is steadier than matching a width that varies with what's
    inside it.

    The bracket is the WHOTITLE column, not a level. It reads
    "<lvl> <race> <class>" about two thirds of the time and something like
    "***ROADHOUSE***" or "*Daily Blessing*" the rest, so it's split only when
    it actually has that shape.
]]
local function parse_line(line)
    if string.len(line) < 18 then return nil end
    if string.sub(line, 1, 1) ~= "[" then return nil end
    if string.sub(line, 17, 17) ~= "]" then return nil end

    local info = trim(string.sub(line, 2, 16))
    local body = trim(string.sub(line, 18))
    if body == "" then return nil end

    --[[
        Peel [Rank] brackets and flags off the front, in any order, until the
        name leads. Safe because clan tags trail the title rather than lead it.
    ]]
    local ranks = {}
    local changed = true
    local guard = 0

    while changed do
        changed = false

        -- belt and braces: a peel that stops shrinking the string would spin
        -- here too, and a locked client is not a failure worth risking twice
        guard = guard + 1
        if guard > 12 then break end

        --[[
            Sliced, not matched. A two-capture string.match does not reliably
            return both here — the level/race/class split lost its third
            capture and came out as "51 Diva undefined".
        ]]
        if string.sub(body, 1, 1) == "[" then
            local close = string.find(body, "]", 1, true)
            if close and close > 2 then
                table.insert(ranks, trim(string.sub(body, 2, close - 1)))
                body = trim(string.sub(body, close + 1))
                changed = true
            end
        end

        for _, f in ipairs(FLAGS) do
            if starts_with(body, f) then
                body = trim(string.sub(body, string.len(f) + 1))
                changed = true
            end
        end
    end

    -- rightmost decoration wins; see the note on DECOR
    local title, clan, cut = body, "", nil

    for _, d in ipairs(DECOR) do
        local at = rfind(body, d[1])
        if at and (not cut or at > cut) then
            cut, clan = at, d[2]
        end
    end

    if cut then title = trim(string.sub(body, 1, cut - 1)) end

    -- first thing that reads like a name. Some clans put their decoration in
    -- FRONT of the player, which leaves nothing before the cut
    local name = lead_word(title)

    if not name then
        -- some clans put their decoration in FRONT of the player, leaving
        -- nothing before the cut. Skip the first token and try again.
        local rest = words(body)
        if #rest >= 2 then name = lead_word(rest[2]) end
    end

    if not name then return nil end

    --[[
        Split, don't match. The bracket is '<lvl> <race> <class>' about two
        thirds of the time and a badge the rest, and a numeric first token is
        what decides — the same test as before, just without asking a
        three-capture regex to hand back three things.
    ]]
    local level, race, class = 0, "", ""
    local bits = words(info)

    if #bits >= 3 and num(bits[1]) then
        level, race, class = num(bits[1]) or 0, bits[2], bits[3]
    end

    return {
        name  = name,
        level = level,
        race  = race,
        class = class,
        badge = (level > 0) and "" or info,
        title = title,
        clan  = clan,
        flags = table.concat(ranks, " "),
    }
end

local function remember(p)
    local k = key_of(p.name)
    if k == "" then return end

    local was = get_player(k)

    put_player(k, {
        name  = p.name,
        -- a badge line carries no level, so don't overwrite a real one with 0
        level = (p.level > 0) and p.level or ((was and was.level) or 0),
        race  = (p.race ~= "") and p.race or ((was and was.race) or ""),
        class = (p.class ~= "") and p.class or ((was and was.class) or ""),
        title = p.title,
        flags = p.flags,
        -- ROADHOUSE, Fabled, SUPERHEROINE: the bracket carries a badge instead
        -- of a level for these, and it's the only place that says so
        badge = (p.badge ~= "") and p.badge or ((was and was.badge) or ""),
        -- keep a clan an earlier sweep learned when this row shows none, but
        -- never leave it nil: unclanned players need the key too
        clan  = (p.clan ~= "") and p.clan or ((was and was.clan) or ""),
        seen  = ((was and was.seen) or 0) + 1,
        at    = getCurrentTime(),
    })

    dirty = true
end

------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- UI
------------------------------------------------------------------------------

local CSS = [[
<style>
    .arc-w {
        font-family: "JetBrains Mono", ui-monospace, monospace;
        color: hsl(var(--foreground, 35 34% 78%));
        height: 100%; box-sizing: border-box;
        display: flex; flex-direction: column;
        background:
            radial-gradient(120% 110% at 15% -10%, rgba(147,25,24,0.13), transparent 60%),
            hsl(var(--card, 0 12% 8%));
        border: 1px solid hsl(var(--border, 0 22% 17%));
        border-radius: var(--glass-radius, 4px);
    }
    .arc-w .bar {
        display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 5px; flex-wrap: wrap;
        padding: 7px 9px;
        border-bottom: 1px solid hsl(var(--border, 0 22% 17%));
    }
    .arc-w .stat {
        font-size: 9px; letter-spacing: 0.06em;
        color: hsl(var(--muted-foreground, 35 14% 52%));
        font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums;
    }
    .arc-w .stat b {
        color: hsl(var(--foreground, 35 34% 78%));
        font-weight: normal; font-size: 11px;
    }
    /*
        The dot sits beside an 11px number, and vertical-align:middle aligns it
        to the middle of the LOWERCASE x-height rather than the middle of the
        digits — so it rode high and looked like a typo. Flex centres it
        against the actual line box instead.
    */
    .arc-w .stat { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; }
    .arc-w .stat .dot {
        width: 6px; height: 6px; border-radius: 50%; flex: none;

local function online_set()
    local on = {}
    for _, n in ipairs(sweep.names) do on[key_of(n)] = true end
    return on
end

local function by_name(a, b)
    return string.lower(a.name) < string.lower(b.name)
end

--[[
    Who to show: the last sweep by default, everything ever seen when there's a
    search. Searching only the online list would make the history unreachable,
    which is most of what a tracker is for.

    Sorted by name either way. The MUD returns who in its own order — roughly
    by level band — which is fine to read top to bottom but useless for finding
    one person, and the list is only ever scanned for a person.
]]
local function rows_for()
    local q = string.lower(trim(cfg.query or ""))
    local out = {}

    if q == "" then
        --[[
            Grouped by bucket before looking anything up.

            Name order is not bucket order: Akira, Betrayal, Argent walk a, b, a
            — and with two buckets held that reloads and evicts the same letters
            over and over, on a list that redraws every sweep. Gathering the
            names per letter first means each bucket is decoded once.
        ]]
        local byLetter = {}
        for _, n in ipairs(sweep.names) do
            local k = key_of(n)
            if k ~= "" then
                local letter = bucket_of(k)
                byLetter[letter] = byLetter[letter] or {}
                table.insert(byLetter[letter], k)
            end
        end

        for _, letter in ipairs(BUCKETS) do
            local keys = byLetter[letter]
            if keys then
                local t = load_bucket(letter)
                for _, k in ipairs(keys) do
                    if t[k] then table.insert(out, t[k]) end
                end
            end
        end

        table.sort(out, by_name)
        return out, false
    end

    --[[
        Walked, not held. One bucket is decoded, searched and released before
        the next is touched, so a search costs one bucket no matter how many
        players have ever been seen.
    ]]
    for _, letter in ipairs(BUCKETS) do
        for _, p in pairs(load_bucket(letter)) do
            local hay = string.lower(p.name .. " " .. (p.title or "") .. " "
                .. (p.race or "") .. " " .. (p.class or "") .. " " .. (p.clan or ""))
            if string.find(hay, q, 1, true) then table.insert(out, p) end
        end
    end

    table.sort(out, by_name)
    return out, true
end

local function render()
    if not widget then return end

    local on = online_set()
    local list, searching = rows_for()

    --[[
        How long ago the sweep was. A restored list looks exactly like a fresh
        one, and 'online' here has only ever meant 'in the most recent sweep'.
    ]]
    local age = ""
    if num(sweep.at) and sweep.at > 0 then
        local mins = math.floor((getCurrentTime() - sweep.at) / 60000)
        if mins >= 1 then
            age = (mins >= 60) and (math.floor(mins / 60) .. "h ago") or (mins .. "m ago")
        end
    end

    -- Online, and nothing else. Peak and connections are reboot trivia; they
    -- belong behind the gear rather than across the top of the list.
    --[[
        A dot rather than the word. "ONLINE 80" spends eleven characters saying
        one thing, and this panel is usually docked in a narrow column where
        that is the difference between the count and the WHO button sharing a
        line. Green means the same thing and costs one.

        title= carries the word for anyone who needs it spelled out.
    ]]
    local bar = '<div class="stat" title="players online at the last sweep">'
        .. '<span class="dot"></span><b>' .. commas(#sweep.names) .. '</b></div>' 
    bar = bar .. '<div class="sp"></div>'
        .. '<div class="tb" data-mud-action="sweep">who</div>'
        .. '<div class="tb' .. (view == "settings" and " on" or "")
        .. '" data-mud-action="view">⚙</div>'

    if view == "settings" then
        local body = '<div class="sec">Sweeps</div>'
            .. '<div class="bar" style="padding:0;border:0">'
            .. '<div class="tb' .. (cfg.poll and " on" or "") .. '" data-mud-action="poll">'
            .. (cfg.poll and ("every " .. cfg.mins .. " min") or "off") .. '</div>'
            .. '<div class="tb" data-mud-action="less">−</div>'
            .. '<div class="tb" data-mud-action="more">+</div>'
            .. '<div class="tb' .. (cfg.gag and " on" or "") .. '" data-mud-action="gag">'
            .. 'hide output</div>'
            .. '</div>'
            .. '<div class="note">Sends <code>who</code> on a timer and reads the reply. '
            .. '<b>Hide output</b> keeps those sweeps out of the terminal — a who you '
            .. 'type yourself is never hidden.</div>'
            .. '<div class="sec">Last sweep</div>'
            .. '<div class="note">' .. commas(#sweep.names) .. ' online'
            .. ((age ~= "") and (", swept " .. age) or "")
            .. ((sweep.max > 0) and ('. Peak this reboot ' .. commas(sweep.max)) or "")
            .. ((sweep.conns > 0) and (', ' .. commas(sweep.conns) .. ' connections') or "")
            .. '.</div>' 
            .. '<div class="sec">Records</div>'
            .. '<div class="note">' .. commas(sweep.tracked or 0)
            .. ' player(s) remembered. Search matches name, title, race and class '
            .. 'across all of them, not just whoever is online.</div>'
            .. '<div class="bar" style="padding:0;border:0">'
            .. '<div class="tb" data-mud-action="forget">forget all</div></div>'
            .. '<div class="sec">Diagnostics</div>'
            .. '<div class="note">onLine fired <b>' .. commas(dbg.lines) .. '</b> time(s), '
            .. 'saw <b>' .. commas(dbg.heads) .. '</b> who header(s), parsed <b>'
            .. commas(dbg.rows) .. '</b> player line(s).'
            .. (dbg.lines == 0
                and ' <b>Zero lines means this plugin never sees the output.</b>'
                or ((dbg.heads > 0 and dbg.rows == 0)
                    and ' <b>Headers but no rows: the line format is not matching.</b>'
                    or ((dbg.heads == 0)
                        and ' <b>Lines but no header: the header text is not matching.</b>'
                        or ""))) .. '</div>'
            .. '<div class="note">Last line seen: <code>'
            .. esc(string.sub(dbg.last or "(none)", 1, 70)) .. '</code></div>'

        setWidgetProperty(widget, "content", CSS
            .. '<div class="arc-w"><div class="bar">' .. bar .. '</div>'
            .. '<div class="body">' .. body .. '</div></div>')
        return
    end

    local body = '<form data-mud-action="find">'
        .. '<input type="text" name="q" placeholder="search name, title, class..." value="'
        .. esc(cfg.query or "") .. '">'
        .. '<button type="submit">find</button></form>'

    if #list == 0 then
        body = body .. '<div class="empty">'
            .. (searching and "Nobody matches that" or "No sweep yet — press WHO")
            .. '</div>'
    end

    local shown = 0
    for _, p in ipairs(list) do
        if shown >= MAX_ROWS then break end
        shown = shown + 1

        --[[
            Name and title, nothing else.

            Level, race, class and clan are all still searched — they're just
            not worth the width. A who list is read to find a person, and the
            name is what you're scanning for.
        ]]
        -- renamed off a file-scope name: shadowing one can fail the whole
        -- plugin load. See NOTES 9b.
        local rest = p.title or ""
        if starts_with(rest, p.name) then
            rest = trim(string.sub(rest, string.len(p.name) + 1))
        end

        body = body .. '<div class="p' .. (on[key_of(p.name)] and " on" or "") .. '">'
            .. '<div class="p1">'
            .. '<span class="nm">' .. esc(p.name) .. '</span>'
            .. '<span class="ti">' .. esc(rest) .. '</span>'
            .. '</div><div class="p2">'
            .. '<span class="go" data-mud-action="whois" data-mud-data="' .. esc(p.name) .. '">whois</span>'
            .. '<span class="go" data-mud-action="finger" data-mud-data="' .. esc(p.name) .. '">finger</span>'
            .. '</div></div>'
    end

    if #list > shown then
        body = body .. '<div class="note">' .. commas(#list - shown)
            .. ' more — narrow the search to see them.</div>'
    end

    setWidgetProperty(widget, "content", CSS
        .. '<div class="arc-w"><div class="bar">' .. bar .. '</div>'
        .. '<div class="body">' .. body .. '</div></div>')
end

------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- the sweep
------------------------------------------------------------------------------

local function count_tracked()
    sweep.tracked = playerN
end

local function do_sweep()
    auto = true
    send("who")

    --[[
        Safety net. If the reply never comes — disconnected, or the MUD too
        busy — auto would stay set and silently eat the next 'who' you typed
        yourself. Ten seconds is far longer than a sweep takes.
    ]]
    setTimeout(function()
        if auto and not inSweep and not tail then auto = false end
    end, 10000)
end

--[[
    Everything happens here, gagging included.

    A line dropped from onLine fires no triggers, so parsing in a trigger and
    gagging here would mean a hidden sweep is also an unread one. Both jobs,
    one pass.

    Only OUR sweeps are hidden: a 'who' you typed is something you asked to
    see, and silently eating it would be the plugin overruling you.
]]
--[[
    onLine(sessionId, rawLine, cleanLine) — THREE arguments, and the first is
    the session, not the text.

    Written as onLine(line) this matched against 'session-1785816768709-k8wpur'
    on every call: 50 lines seen, 0 headers, 0 players, and no error anywhere.
    Comms has had the right signature all along; I didn't look.

    cleanLine arrives already stripped of colour, which matters because every
    pattern here is anchored at ^ and an escape sequence in front of the
    bracket means nothing ever matches.
]]
function onLine(sessionId, rawLine, cleanLine)
    local clean = cleanLine
    if type(clean) ~= "string" then clean = stripAnsiCodes(rawLine) end
    if type(clean) ~= "string" then clean = rawLine end
    if type(clean) ~= "string" then return end

    dbg.lines = dbg.lines + 1
    dbg.last = clean

    local hide = auto and cfg.gag

    if string.find(clean, "Aardwolf Players Online", 1, true) then
        dbg.heads = dbg.heads + 1
        inSweep = true
        tail = false
        sweep.names = {}
        return not hide
    end

    --[[
        The block does not end at 'Players found:'. Aardwolf follows it with

            Players found: [88], Max this reboot: [232], Connections...
            Players invis: [116], Max on ever: [853]

        and the second line escaped the gag entirely, so an automatic sweep
        still put a stray line on screen. Anything starting 'Players ' is part
        of the tail; the first line that isn't ends the block.
    ]]
    if tail then
        if string.sub(clean, 1, 8) == "Players " then
            return not hide
        end

        tail = false
        auto = false
        return
    end

    if not inSweep then return end

    local found = string.match(clean, "^Players found: *\\[?(\\d+)")
    if type(found) == "string" then
        sweep.found = num(found) or 0
        sweep.at = getCurrentTime()

        local mx = string.match(clean, "Max this reboot: *\\[?(\\d+)")
        local cn = string.match(clean, "Connections this reboot: *\\[?(\\d+)")
        if type(mx) == "string" then sweep.max = num(mx) or sweep.max end
        if type(cn) == "string" then sweep.conns = num(cn) or sweep.conns end

        inSweep = false
        tail = true

        count_tracked()
        save_db()
        save_sweep()
        render()

        return not hide
    end

    --[[
        pcall, and a cap.

        This parser has locked the client twice. A throw here would kill the
        sweep silently; a runaway takes the whole client with nothing to read
        afterwards. Neither is worth risking again for a who list.
    ]]
    if #sweep.names > 600 then
        if hide then return false end
        return
    end

    local pok, p = pcall(function() return parse_line(clean) end)
    if not pok then
        dbg.errs = (dbg.errs or 0) + 1
        p = nil
    end

    if p then
        dbg.rows = dbg.rows + 1
        remember(p)
        table.insert(sweep.names, p.name)
        return not hide
    end

    --[[
        Everything else between the header and the footer: the 'Use swho'
        hint, the rules, anything Aardwolf adds later. An automatic sweep hides
        the whole block, not the parts we happen to recognise — a line we
        didn't anticipate appearing on its own is exactly what "gag the output"
        is meant to prevent.
    ]]
    if hide then return false end
end

------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- lifecycle
------------------------------------------------------------------------------

local pollTimer = nil

local function arm_poll()
    if pollTimer then
        removeTimer(pollTimer)
        pollTimer = nil
    end

    if not cfg.poll then return end

    -- milliseconds: addTimer(1, ...) measured 21ms between ticks, so it is not
    -- the seconds the name suggests
    pollTimer = addTimer(cfg.mins * 60000, do_sweep, true)
end

function init()
    widget = createWidget({
        type     = "html",
        name     = "who",
        title    = "Players",
        position = { x = 640, y = 60 },
        size     = { width = 460, height = 420 },
        --[[
            No title bar. Every panel here draws its own header with its own
            controls, so the client's chrome was a second title above ours
            saying the same thing.

            This is a plugin DEFAULT, not a lock — it's declared through the
            appearance table at creation, which the user can still override in
            the widget's own cog. autoHideSettingsCog keeps that cog reachable
            on hover rather than it going away with the bar.
        ]]
        appearance = {
            showTitleBar        = false,
            autoHideSettingsCog = true,
        },
    })

    local saved = loadTable("aw_who")

    if type(saved) ~= "table" then
        local ok, raw = pcall(function() return getVariable("aw_who_cfg") end)
        if ok and type(raw) == "string" and raw ~= "" then
            local dok, data = pcall(json.decode, raw)
            if dok and type(data) == "table" then saved = data end
        end
    end

    if type(saved) == "table" then
        if saved.poll == true then cfg.poll = true end
        if saved.gag == false then cfg.gag = false end
        if num(saved.mins) and num(saved.mins) >= 1 then cfg.mins = num(saved.mins) end
    end

    -- the backup is only written on save, so a fresh install has none until
    -- something changes. Write one now.
    save_cfg()

    local n = load_db()
    load_sweep()
    count_tracked()

    if n > 0 then
        utilprint(TAG .. "remembering " .. commas(n) .. " player(s).")
    end

    --[[
        Clear first. init() runs again on every hot-reload and
        registerWidgetEvent APPENDS — so each reload stacks another handler on
        the same widget and one click fires all of them. It shows up as buttons
        sending their command two, three, five times, getting worse the longer
        a session goes on, and nothing about it looks like a plugin bug from
        the outside.

        unregisterWidgetEvent with no callback drops every handler for the
        event, which is exactly what a fresh init wants.
    ]]
    drop_handlers(widget, "action")
    registerWidgetEvent(widget, "action", function(data)
        if type(data) ~= "table" then return end

        local act = tostring(data.action or "")
        local arg = tostring(data.data or "")

        if act == "whois" then
            send("whois " .. arg)
            return

        elseif act == "finger" then
            send("finger " .. arg)
            return

        elseif act == "sweep" then
            do_sweep()
            return

        elseif act == "view" then
            view = (view == "settings") and "list" or "settings"

        elseif act == "poll" then
            cfg.poll = not cfg.poll
            save_cfg()
            arm_poll()

        elseif act == "gag" then
            cfg.gag = not cfg.gag
            save_cfg()

        elseif act == "more" then
            cfg.mins = cfg.mins + 5
            save_cfg()
            arm_poll()

        elseif act == "less" then
            cfg.mins = (cfg.mins > 5) and (cfg.mins - 5) or 1
            save_cfg()
            arm_poll()

        elseif act == "forget" then
            -- every bucket, not one table
            for _, letter in ipairs(BUCKETS) do
                bkt[letter] = {}
                bktDirty[letter] = true
            end
            playerN = 0

            sweep.names = {}
            dirty = true
            count_tracked()
            save_db()
            save_sweep()

        else
            return
        end

        render()
    end)

    --[[
        Form submits carry every named field, which is how a search box works
        without any JavaScript in the widget.
    ]]
    drop_handlers(widget, "submit")
    registerWidgetEvent(widget, "submit", function(data)
        if type(data) ~= "table" then return end

        local f = data.formData
        if type(f) ~= "table" then return end

        cfg.query = trim(tostring(f.q or ""))
        render()
    end)

    arm_poll()
    render()
end

function cleanup()
    dirty = true
    save_db()
    save_sweep()
end

local function help_text()
    utilprint(TAG .. "who list, player history and timed sweeps.")
    utilprint("$w  /players                       this help")
    utilprint("$w  /players sweep                 send a who now and read the reply")
    utilprint("$w  /players <text>                search name, title, race, class, clan")
    utilprint("$w  /players <minutes>             sweep on a timer, e.g. '/players 15'")
    utilprint("$w  /players off                   stop the timer")
    utilprint(TAG .. commas(sweep.found or 0) .. " online at the last sweep, "
        .. commas(sweep.tracked or 0) .. " player(s) remembered."
        .. (cfg.poll and ("  Sweeping every " .. cfg.mins .. " min.") or "  Timer off."))
end

registerCommand("players", function(args)
    local a = trim(tostring(args or ""))
    local sub = string.lower(a)

    --[[
        A bare command shows help. It used to send a who sweep, which is a
        command going to the MUD because you typed the plugin's name and
        nothing else — surprising, and not what anyone means by '/players'.
        '/players sweep' still does it.
    ]]
    if sub == "" or sub == "help" then
        help_text()
        return
    end

    if sub == "sweep" or sub == "who" then
        do_sweep()
        return
    end

    if sub == "off" then
        cfg.poll = false
        save_cfg()
        arm_poll()
        utilprint(TAG .. "sweeps off.")
        return
    end

    local mins = num(sub)
    if mins and mins >= 1 then
        cfg.mins = math.floor(mins)
        cfg.poll = true
        save_cfg()
        arm_poll()
        utilprint(TAG .. "sweeping every " .. cfg.mins .. " minute(s).")
        return
    end

    -- anything else is a search
    cfg.query = a
    view = "list"
    render()
    utilprint(TAG .. "searching for '" .. a .. "'.")
end, "Who list and player history. '/players' for help, '/players sweep' sweeps now, '/players <text>' searches")
